title: Cosmic Soil Upgrade — Density-Ratio Fixed Points, Scaling Solutions and Stability Verdict
status: archive-generated analytical continuation of the explicit Cosmic Soil interacting-dark-sector benchmark; phenomenological cosmology, not recovered Great Book mathematics
abstract: The selected Cosmic Soil benchmark Q=xi H rho_c can be reduced to an exact autonomous equation for the dark-matter to dark-energy density ratio r=rho_c/rho_de. This reveals whether the interaction naturally produces a persistent scaling balance. The analysis gives two fixed points, an exact local-stability criterion and a useful negative result: for a constant negative-pressure dark-energy equation of state w<0 under the benchmark sign convention, every physically positive nonzero scaling fixed point requires xi>0 and is locally unstable. In particular, for w=-1 the model flows toward dark-energy domination for the ordinary small-coupling regime rather than toward a stable O(1) dark-sector ratio. Thus the simplest Q proportional to H rho_c coupling does not automatically solve the coincidence problem even though it admits a formal constant-ratio branch.

conventions.interaction: Q=xi H rho_c with xi>0 meaning background energy transfer from dark energy to cold dark matter in this archive convention.
conventions.ratio: r=rho_c/rho_de, restricted to rho_de>0 when interpreted physically.

result_1_ratio_equation.value: The two-component background ratio can therefore be studied without integrating both densities separately.

result_2_fixed_points.existence_condition: The scaling point is physically admissible only when r_star>0 and both component densities remain positive in the epoch being modeled.
result_2_fixed_points.constant_ratio_meaning: At r_star the two dark densities dilute with the same effective power of a, so their ratio remains constant.

result_3_local_stability.derivative_at_zero: f'(0)=3w+xi. Thus r=0 is locally stable for 3w+xi<0 and unstable for 3w+xi>0.
result_3_local_stability.stability_condition_scaling: A positive scaling fixed point is locally stable only if xi<0.
result_3_local_stability.negative_pressure_consequence: For w<0, r_star>0 implies xi>0 with xi<-3w. Therefore the physically positive scaling point is necessarily unstable in this simple constant-w benchmark.
result_3_local_stability.project_result: The model can possess a formal dark-sector balance without that balance being a late-time attractor.

result_4_scaling_equation_of_state.common_dilution: rho_dark at the scaling point therefore follows a^[-3(1+w_eff)]=a^(-3+xi), matching the dark-matter dilution exponent.
result_4_scaling_equation_of_state.acceleration_condition: A scaling branch would require w_eff<-1/3, hence xi>1, for accelerated expansion in this simplified dark-sector-only criterion.
result_4_scaling_equation_of_state.warning: Acceleration of the full cosmology depends on all components and the physical viability of the branch, not this algebraic condition alone.

w_minus_one_case.stability: f'(r_star)=xi r_star>0 throughout that positive range, so the scaling point is unstable.
w_minus_one_case.dark_energy_point: r=0 is stable for xi<3 because f'(0)=-3+xi<0.
w_minus_one_case.verdict: For the ordinary positive-coupling range 0<xi<3, the system tends toward dark-energy domination rather than a stable nonzero matter/dark-energy ratio.

phase_line_interpretation.below_unstable_scaling: When 0<r<r_star in the w=-1, 0<xi<3 case, f(r)<0 and the ratio decreases toward zero.
phase_line_interpretation.above_unstable_scaling: When r>r_star, f(r)>0 and the ratio grows away from the scaling point within the reduced background model.
phase_line_interpretation.boundary: Global physical evolution must still respect positivity, early-universe constraints and the validity of the constant-w phenomenological interaction.

scientific_contribution.positive: The interaction law is now linked to a phase portrait and explicit attractor question rather than only analytic density formulas.
scientific_contribution.negative: The simplest selected coupling does not provide a stable positive scaling solution for the physically relevant constant negative-pressure branch.
scientific_contribution.research_direction: A stable coincidence-motivated attractor, if desired, requires a different interaction structure, dynamical dark-energy field, additional degrees of freedom or a different sign/model—not reinterpretation of this unstable point.

external_references.topic: fixed points in interacting dark energy
external_references.use: Established phase-plane/fixed-point methodology and demonstration that scaling attractors depend on the specific interaction model.

failure_conditions: The unstable positive scaling point is described as a late-time attractor.
A fixed-ratio background solution is treated as perturbatively stable without solving perturbations.
The negative result is hidden by switching interaction sign conventions without explicitly redefining Q.
A different interaction law is introduced solely to force a desired coincidence result without independent motivation or comparison.
